declarations.docstring: The degree-n k-module obtained from the linear Yoneda complex associated to a projective resolution and a coefficient module.
The degree-n additive commutative group attached to a left module and a projective resolution of an opposite-ring module.
A morphism between projective resolution complexes induces a morphism between their linear Yoneda complexes in the reversed direction.
The degree-n linear Yoneda homology modules obtained from two projective resolutions are isomorphic.
A morphism of projective resolution complexes induces a map on the degree-n linear Yoneda homology modules.
A resolution morphism compatible with the augmentations induces the hom of the canonical linear Yoneda homology isomorphism.
Two resolution morphisms compatible with the augmentations induce the same map on linear Yoneda homology.
The linear Yoneda complexes associated to two projective resolutions are homotopy equivalent.
The homology map induced by a compatible morphism of projective resolutions is the hom of the comparison isomorphism after applying an additive functor.
Compatible morphisms between the same projective resolutions induce equal homology maps after applying an additive functor.
Applying an additive functor to two projective resolutions gives canonically isomorphic homology objects in every degree.
The hom of the additive-functor homology comparison isomorphism from a projective resolution to itself is the identity.
The composite of two additive-functor homology comparison isomorphisms agrees with the direct comparison isomorphism.
The degree-n groups attached to a left module and two projective resolutions of an opposite-ring module are isomorphic.
The hom of the module-pair homology comparison isomorphism from a projective resolution to itself is the identity.
The composite of two module-pair homology comparison isomorphisms agrees with the direct comparison isomorphism.
A morphism of projective resolution complexes induces a map on the associated degree-n module-pair homology groups.
A resolution morphism compatible with the augmentations induces the hom of the module-pair homology comparison isomorphism.
Two resolution morphisms compatible with the augmentations induce the same map on module-pair homology.
A homotopy equivalence of complexes in an opposite category yields a reversed homotopy equivalence between their unop complexes.
Any two projective resolutions of the same module have a nonempty type of homotopy equivalences between their complexes.
Between any two projective resolutions of the same module there exists a complex morphism intertwining their augmentations.
